title: The crew member reveals secrets of cruise ships, from the 'dark side' of life as an artist of the 'disorderly truth' about relations on board and what happens when someone dies in the sea …
text:
Have you ever wondered what happens if a passenger dies at sea during a cruise? Or if the crew members can leave each other?
You will find the answers below and more also, such as Lauren Heavner ( @Laurenheav ), A professional vocalist who has worked on cruises for more than 10 years for six different lines in more than 1,000 trips, reveals a large number of cruise secrets.
Move down and also discover the sad truth about whales by hitting ships and how Lauren faces love guests …
The ships have a small hospital of doctors and nurses
The aid is never far if you are wrong at sea.
Lauren tells Mailonline Travel: ‘On a cruise, the size of the medical installation is a game of numbers: guest numbers, to be exact.
‘For a giant with 4,000 guests, you will generally find two doctors and a small six or seven nurses battalion to handle everything, from dizziness to something more sinister.
“But in smaller and intimate ships, for example, those who amazed less than 1,000 guests are looking at a thinner operation: a doctor, a couple of nurses and the hope that everyone’s sunscreen game is strong” .
Norovirus extends faster than the gossip
Lauren Heavner, in the photo above, is a professional vocalist on cruises. She has shared internal knowledge about life at sea with Mailonline
The cruise artist reveals that the vomiting error is a real plague in the sea.
She says: ‘Over the years, I have seen my part of medical emergencies in cruises, too many falls that end in broken bones, a couple of heart attacks that charged lives and norovirus outbreaks that extended faster than gossip in The crew bar. ‘
The ocean humiliate everyone
Lauren explains: ‘It doesn’t matter if you are an experienced rookie or sailor, the ocean has a way to humiliate everyone. Dizziness is, with much, the most common reason for a trip to the medical installation of the ship.
Certain cruises tend to see more medical emergencies
“Medical emergencies on board are not exactly a daily fact, but they are not rare,” explains Lauren. “Certain cruises, or more precise, certain lines, tend to see more than their part, based on the demography of their passengers.”
She reveals: ‘I even had my own touch with the disaster once. If you are out there, Doc, I owe you a drink or two.
The ships have a morgue
If the worst happens, and “someone goes to the sea,” Lauren explains that “the process is handled with a quiet professionalism.”
She says: ‘The cruise line notifies the family, offering comfort and support. If the ship is far from the port, the body is stored respectfully in the morgue of the ship.
“Once on land, arrangements are made to repatriate the deceased, ensuring that they return home with dignity.”
COVID-19 It was like a nightmare
Lauren explains that ‘he faces the strange inappropriate comment of men’ and says that Covid-19 was “terrifying” for crew. Left: Lauren on a cruise. Right: isolated during pandemic
Lauren tells Mailonline: ‘Nothing compares with Covid-19 chaos. Being a member of the crew on a cruise during that time was like living a nightmare without the shore in sight.
‘Isolation, fear and uncertainty hung in the air as heavy as ocean fog. It was not just scary, it was the type of terrible that leaves a brand, of the guy you carry with you long after the seas has calmed down.
Passenger/crew relations happen
The professional vocalist tells Mailonline: ‘Fraternize with passengers is strictly prohibited for crew members, a rule that comes with one of the hardest consequences: immediate termination.
‘But the rules, as we all know, are as strong as the people who follow them. And let’s say not everyone on the ship are fans of playing next to the book.
There is a darker side of life as an artist
Lauren explains that as a ‘main artist’, he is often ‘the face of the ship’. She shows up on a show on board
The vocalist reveals that working as an interpreter comes with ‘his part of advantages and peculiarities’. She shows up with other cast members and the West End and Broadway Elaine Page star after a show after a show
Lauren is photographed with a ship in Sydney, Australia
Lauren does not entertain inappropriate comments.
She reveals: ‘As the main artist, I am often the face of the ship, a role that comes with its share of advantages and peculiarities.
‘Guests love to chat, share a drink or stay during dinner, soak in a little of that magic of Spotlight. But there is a darker side in attention.
‘The strange inappropriate comment of men is, unfortunately, part of the work. Over time, I have dominated the art of the fast counter: firm, humorous, respectful, but enough to remind you that you have not wanted. “
There is a disorderly truth in crew relationships
Lauren explains: ‘The relations between crew members are as common as the sunsets in the sea, a natural by -product of closed rooms and long contracts. But under the surface there is a more messy truth.
‘The real question is not whether they are in a relationship, it is whether their spouses at home know it.
‘Of course, there are genuine and monogamous relationships in ships, based on something real. But let’s not fool ourselves, those are the exceptions, not the rule.
She adds: ‘Crew members are free to leave each other, it is practically inevitable in the very close world of the ship’s life.
“But there is a hard and fast warning: there are no relationships between a supervisor and its subordinates.”
GLOBETROTTER LAUREN is shown here in Malta, in the blue lagoon of the island
The captain establishes the tone for the ship
Lauren tells Mailonline that the captain often establishes the atmosphere in a ship, revealing: ‘Everything is reduced to the personality of the captain. Some prefer to maintain a low profile, just appear for mandatory events.
‘Others are the opposite: extroverted, accessible and anxious to connect with the crew. Each captain brings their own style to the bridge, and establish the tone for the entire ship.
The ships hit whales
The professional vocalist explains: ‘He was on a ship that crossed Alaska when we hit a whale, a collision that left the whale covered on the bow of the ship when we arrived at the port. This quickly reached national headlines.
“The reactions of the passengers and the crew were surprisingly similar: impotence mixed with a disturbing sense of guilt, even though it was beyond the control of anyone.”
